All national parks / Yellowstone & Grand Teton: a four-day route

WYOMING · MONTANA · IDAHO

Grand Teton

Volcanic plateaus, colorful hot springs and fault-block mountains. Start and finish in Bozeman, linking two neighboring yet very different parks through scenic drives, short trails and visitor centers.

Colter Bay & visitor centerJackson Lake DamOxbow BendJenny Lake & visitor centerMormon Row Historic DistrictVisitor centers & badges

Understanding this park

Movement along the Teton fault displaced the mountains and basin relative to each other; glaciers then carved valleys and lakes. Unlike Yellowstone’s thermal focus, this park centers on steep peaks, lakeshores and the Snake River. A short visit can focus on the northern lake area; Jenny Lake, Mormon Row and boat outings fit better into a separate day.

Colter Bay & visitor center

Forested shores and sheltered bays on Jackson Lake form a northern introduction to the Tetons. Start with exhibits and lakeside views, then decide how far south to continue.

Allow roughly 30–45 minutes for a short visit. The visitor center is seasonal; ask about park information, badges and that day’s desk hours.

Jackson Lake Dam

Glaciers shaped the lake basin, while the modern dam changed water-level management. Water, mountain faces and the outlet show natural landforms alongside human water use.

A roughly 15–20-minute roadside stop works well. Use legal parking and respect road and dam facility restrictions.

Oxbow Bend

A bend in the Snake River frames distant peaks in a classic Teton landscape. Calm conditions may produce reflections; wind and water levels change the scene.

Allow roughly 15–30 minutes for views and photos. Reflections and wildlife are not guaranteed. This can be the last stop before turning north for a night in Canyon.

Jenny Lake & visitor center

Valley glaciers eroded basins and moved debris, leaving the lake and moraines. Close views of the mountain base, water and forest offer a different scale from highway overlooks.

The paved Discovery Trail is about 0.56 km. A 30–45-minute visit covers only the lakeshore and visitor center. A boat outing to Hidden Falls or Inspiration Point needs several additional hours.

Mormon Row Historic District

Historic barns set against the Tetons create an iconic composition and record the lives of early farming communities. These buildings are part of a cultural landscape, not natural formations.

Allow roughly 30–45 minutes, adjusting for road and parking conditions. This is a southern extension; if returning to Yellowstone the same day, save it for an additional day.

Passport stamps & Junior Ranger: visit during staffed hours

In Grand Teton, consider Jenny Lake or Colter Bay visitor centers and check seasonal staffing. Jenny Lake’s official page welcomes all ages to Junior Ranger. Activities and review take time; reserve a separate 20–30-minute desk visit.

Official information & before you go

This route is for the season when main roads are open. Times are planning estimates, not guarantees, and do not include every parking, traffic or weather delay. Check seasonal roads, trails and visitor-center hours before departure.
